newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania PM predicts NATO membership next time.
newsitem.headline: Romania PM predicts NATO membership next time.

text.p: Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said Romania had failed in its bid for early NATO membership because of delays in implementing post-communist reforms but predicted it would be accepted in the next expansion wave.

"Romania's efforts to promote reforms are clear to all and lead us to a clear conclusion," he told a Romanian television station from a conference north of Bucharest. "If we complete reforms, and I'm sure we will, in 1999 we'll be NATO members."

NATO's 16 leaders announced in Madrid that Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic had been invited to join the alliance. But the summit left the door open for a review of further expansion in 1999 and specifically praised the efforts of Romania and Slovenia.

Romanian President Emil Constantinescu had all but abandoned hope of securing first-wave admission and had argued instead for a "reasonable compromise", giving assurances that countries turned away would be considered later.

Ciorbea told Romanian radio that his centrist government could not in seven months in office close the economic gap with the three more advanced neighbours after seven years of slow reforms under ex-communists.
"We all wish we were part of the first wave but we must admit that although in the past seven months we did everything humanly possible, we could not catch up the years of delay," he said.
